subject: Re: ACME bake-off / next steps and test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anika Nguyen <anika@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00Z
Subject: ACME bake-off — post-call recap and proposed test plan

Hi Anika,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear more about ACME's latency-sensitive document ingestion use case and the volume profile (spiky batch loads during market open). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the bake-off: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: reduce inference unit cost while meeting 100ms p90 latency for short (<256 token) responses and 500ms p95 for longer runs.
- Secondary: embedding accuracy for rerank pipeline (MRR target >0.78 vs baseline).
- Constraint: must run within your VPC for the pilot (data residency).

Proposed competitive bake-off scope
1) Test matrix: Redwood Hosted (prod model), Redwood Private (on your VPC), AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI — run identical prompts/datasets.
2) Metrics: latency distribution (p50/p90/p95), throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1M tokens, embedding MRR/recall on labeled eval set, failure rate and error classification.
3) Success criteria: Redwood meets latency SLOs AND achieves embedding MRR within 3% of your current baseline while demonstrating cost <= 0.75x of your current spend.
4) Timeline: kickoff next Tue (2026-11-17), 2-week test window, deliverable: final bake-off report + recommendations.

I've attached a starter test-plan spreadsheet with proposed test cases, owners, and data pointers. Next actions I propose: 
- You: confirm the evaluation team and provide access to the labeled eval set (or a secure link) and the contact for infrastructure (for VPC setup).
- ACME infra: confirm an allowed maintenance window for installation (if Private).
- Redwood: Aditya will draft the technical test harness and Marcus will coordinate the Dedicated/VPC deployment.

Would love your confirmation on scope and kickoff date.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0162

Attachment: acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Anika Nguyen <anika@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME bake-off — technical test matrix and infra notes

Hi Anika / team — putting a quick technical plan here so infra can scope the VPC steps. Key items: 

Test harness and data- We'll run the same request stream against each provider using your sanitized eval set. Harness will capture per-request token counts, latency, and model outputs for deterministic scoring.

Models and configurations- Redwood: opt into quantized model variant for cost runs; baseline full-precision for quality runs.- Bedrock/Vertex: request comparable model sizes; we'll document exact model IDs used for reproducibility.

VPC steps (high level)
1) ACME provides a peered subnet and a service account (or temporary bastion) for installation.
2) Redwood will provide a bootstrap script and a short list of required ports (SSH, gRPC endpoints) and a list of minimal IAM roles.
3) We'll expose a scoped test API endpoint behind your firewall for the eval harness.

Data handling- All logs and model outputs stored encrypted at rest; we'll provide a logging retention plan and delete raw outputs after the bake-off unless you request otherwise.

I'll draft the exact commands and minimal playbook by EOD Monday (11/16). For performance runs, we'll need a short period of warm-up traffic (10K tokens) to get stable KV cache numbers.

Action items (tentative owners)
- Provide sanitized eval set (ACME / Anika) — due 2026-11-13 EOD
- Provide VPC peering details and infra contact (ACME infra) — due 2026-11-14
- Playbook + harness (Aditya) — due 2026-11-16
- Deployment + monitoring dashboards (Marcus) — due 2026-11-17 (kickoff)

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Thanks all — quick status update and a compressed run-of-show for kickoff on 2026-11-17 (30m):

Kickoff (Tue 11/17) 30m agenda- 0-5m: Introductions and objectives (Marissa)- 5-10m: ACME baseline and constraints (Anika)- 10-15m: Redwood test approach and infra checklist (Aditya)- 15-25m: Deployment timeline + responsibilities (Marcus)- 25-30m: Q/A and next steps (Marissa)

Updated owners and due dates- ACME: sanitize eval set + provide GCS link (Anika) — 11/13 (in flight)- ACME infra: provide peered subnet and infra contact (infra@acme.com) — 11/14- Redwood (Aditya): playbook + test harness repo link — 11/16- Redwood (Marcus): VPC deployment + monitor dashboards ready for warm-up — 11/17
- Redwood (Vanessa): customer success onboarding, coordinate access and meeting invites — 11/16

Success criteria (explicit)- Latency: p90 < 100ms for short queries; p95 < 500ms for long queries- Embedding: MRR >= baseline - 3%- Cost: 1M token cost <= 0.75x ACME baseline (for production-config runs)- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% over test window

Please confirm owners and the kickoff slot — I sent a calendar invite for Tue 11/17 09:00 PT. Marcus, Aditya — please confirm dashboards + playbook deliverables.

Best,
Marissa
